sentence: This project holds a three-day meeting where people present their work and review the methods and results of their peers.
This project builds a functional imaging method that shows how metabolic activity varies across healthy organs and tumor tissue.
This project studies how developmental transcription factors control gene expression and shape the microenvironment during brain tumor development.
This project studies how cancer cells harvest mitochondria from immune cells through nanotubes, and builds exocyst inhibitors to overcome this barrier to immune checkpoint inhibitors.
This project builds sensors and instruments that monitor and image neural activity in freely behaving animals without damage and distortion.
This project studies how nuclear myosins organize chromatin and lead to epigenetic silencing of gene expression as pancreatic cancer develops.
This project designs and tests bacteriophage treatments against multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae and other ESKAPE pathogens using computational modeling and organoid testing.
This project builds a rapid HIV self-test that detects early acute infection and viral rebound in people receiving antiretroviral therapy.
This project examines postmortem brain tissue to learn how Alzheimer's disease mutations lead to amyloid and tau buildup and how astrocytes and microglia respond.
This project tries to find out how liquid-liquid phase separation drives cisplatin resistance in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
This project uses liquid biopsy technology to study how tumor cells with integrated HPV change during treatment failure and how integration forms fusion genes.
This project develops polymeric and lipid nanoparticles that edit genes directly inside blood stem cells in patients.
This project tests ways to target transcriptional co-activators, including PGC-1β signaling, to treat metastatic colorectal cancer.
This project studies how JC virus causes Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy and looks for biomarkers and small compounds that can prevent or treat the disease.
This project supports work in genetics and cell biology with direct implications for human health and disease.
This project studies how neuronal activity-responsive regulatory elements differ between humans and other primates, using neuronal cultures and machine learning models.
This project develops an automated platform that images and sections whole mouse brains into thin sections mounted on glass slides for brain mapping.
This project aims to identify substance use needs in communities and to carry out research projects that tackle them.
This project uses genetic crosses to find the molecular changes behind artemisinin resistance in Plasmodium falciparum malaria parasites and their effect on transmission.
This project explores how olfactory receptors change tumor-associated macrophages in melanoma and whether targeting these receptors can activate their anti-tumor function.
